commit_message:
[sfnt] `FT_Load_Sfnt_Table` can now also load a font's table directory.

Closes issue #1263.

* src/sfnt/ttload.c (tt_face_load_any): Implement it.
pr_title: [sfnt] `FT_Load_Sfnt_Table` can now also load a font's table directory.

findings.title: Out-of-Bounds Read in tt_face_load_any via unchecked face_index into ttc_header.offsets
findings.message: In `tt_face_load_any`, when `tag == 1` (table directory access), the code directly uses `face->root.face_index & 0xFFFF` as an index into `face->ttc_header.offsets[]` without first verifying the index is within bounds (`< face->ttc_header.count`). The `face_index` field is also used to enumerate elements of font containers such as Mac Resource files, which are not TTC collections and may therefore have `ttc_header.count == 0` or a very small count. An attacker supplying a crafted font container can cause the index to exceed the allocated `offsets` array, resulting in an out-of-bounds read and potential information disclosure or crash.
findings.suggestion: Before using `face->root.face_index & 0xFFFF` as an index into `face->ttc_header.offsets[]`, check whether the index is less than `face->ttc_header.count`. If the font is not a TTC (or the index is out of range), default to index 0.

ground_truth.root_cause: The code introduced to implement table-directory access (tag == 1) assumed the face is always part of a TTC and that `face_index` is always a valid index into `ttc_header.offsets`. However, `face_index` is also used for non-TTC container formats (e.g., Mac Resource), and no bounds check was added before dereferencing the `offsets` array. The same oversight exists in `sfobjs.c` where a similar condition (`face_index >= face->ttc_header.count`) needed a comment clarifying the context.
